1. Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after recent spikes — adjust downward bias for first 5–7 days.
2. Model overestimates prices after sharp upward moves (e.g., 72+ → 75+), often overshooting by 2–5% — apply dampening factor to post-spike forecasts.
3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — over-predicts correction after peaks, under-predicts recovery after troughs — use moving average of 10–15 days as baseline for adjustment.
4. Forecast lag: model tends to lag true price movements by 2–4 days — shift forecast 1–2 days forward for short-term (next 5–7 days) predictions.
5. Model overreacts to recent volatility — especially in low-price regimes (below 70) — reduce forecast amplitude by 10–15% for periods with high volatility or low historical mean.
6. For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate true mean — add 1–2% to forecast mean to align with historical 30-day average of true outcomes.
